source_text: Εὐφυῶς οὖν ὁ νόμος, ἀπὸ τοῦ συμβαίνειν αὐτοῖς εἰωθότος, τοὺς θείους ἱερουργοὺς ἀνορθοῖ πρὸς τὸ ἄμεινον, καὶ ὡς ἐκ τύπου σωματικοῦ, πρὸς θεωρίαν ἄγει πνευματικήν. «Οὐ» γὰρ «ἀναβήσῃ,» φησὶν, «ἐν ἀναβαθμοῖς ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριόν μου, ἵνα μὴ ἀποκαλύψῃς τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην σου ἐπ' αὐτοῦ.» Τοῦτ' ἔστιν, Ὁ θεῖος ἱερουργὸς ὁ πρὸς λειτουργίαν ἡγιασμένος τὴν ἐμὴν, ζητείτω τὰ ταπεινὰ, μὴ ἀναθρωσκέτω πρὸς τὸ ὑψοῦ. Παραιτείσθω τὴν ἀλαζονείαν, ἵνα μὴ ἀσχήμων ὁρῷτο καὶ ἀκαλλής. Ἀκαλλὲς γὰρ καὶ ἄσχημον κομιδῇ καὶ παγχάλεπον ἀῤῥώστημα νοῦ, φρόνημα τὸ ὑπέρογκον. «Ὅσῳ γὰρ μέγας εἶ, φησὶ, τοσούτῳ ταπείνου σεαυτὸν, καὶ ἔναντι Κυρίου εὑρήσεις χάριν.» Γράφει δὲ καὶ ὁ τοῦ Σωτῆρος μαθητής· «Καυχάσθω ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ· ὁ δὲ πλούσιος, ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει αὐτοῦ.» Παρελεύσεται γὰρ καὶ ἐν ἴσῳ πόαις, καὶ ἀνθέων διοίσει τῶν ἐν ἀγροῖς κατ' οὐδένα τρόπον. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Σύμφημι. {ΚΥΡ.} Ὄγκου δὴ οὖν καὶ ὑπεροψίας ἀπηλλάχθαι δεῖν ἔφη τὸν ἱερουργόν. Τίνα τε οὖν τρόπον ἐννομωτάτην ποιήσαιτο ἂν τὴν ἱερουργίαν καὶ ἀνεπίπληκτον, παντελῶς εἴσῃ τοι σαφῶς· γέγραπται γὰρ ἐν τῷ Λευϊτικῷ· «Καὶ ἐλάλησε Κύριος πρὸς Μωσῆν, λέγων· Ἔντειλαι Ἀαρὼν καὶ τοῖς υἱοῖς αὐτοῦ, λέγων· Οὗτος ὁ νόμος τῆς ὁλοκαυτώσεως, αὕτη ἡ ὁλοκαύτωσις ἐπὶ τῆς καύσεως αὐτῆς ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ὅλην τὴν νύκτα ἕως τοπρωΐ· καὶ τὸ πῦρ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου καυθήσεται ἐπ' αὐτοῦ, οὐ σβεσθήσεται· καὶ ἐνδύσεται ὁ ἱερεὺς χιτῶνα λινοῦν, καὶ περισκελὲς λινοῦν ἐνδύσεται περὶ τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀφελεῖ τὴν κατακάρπωσιν, ἣν ἂν καταναλώσῃ τὸ πῦρ, τὴν ὁλοκαύτωσιν ἀπὸ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, καὶ παραθήσει αὐτὸ ἐχόμενον τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, καὶ ἐκδύσεται τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐνδύσεται στολὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἐξοίσει τὴν κατακάρπωσιν ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς εἰς τόπον καθαρόν· καὶ πῦρ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον καυθήσεται ἐπ' αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐ σβεσθήσεται· καὶ καύσει ἐπ' αὐτοῦ ὁ ἱερεὺς ξύλα τοπρωῒ πρωῒ, καὶ στοιβάσει ἐπ' αὐτοῦ τὴν ὁλοκαύτωσιν, καὶ ἐπιθήσει ἐπ' αὐτὸ τὸ στέαρ τοῦ σωτηρίου καὶ πῦρ διὰ παντὸς καυθήσεται ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον, οὐ σβεσθήσεται.» Ἐνδελεχὲς μὲν οὖν καὶ ἀκατάπαυστον κομιδῇ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου τὸ πῦρ, καὶ οὐκ ὀθνεῖον ἢ ἔξωθεν, ἀλλὰ τὸ αὐτοῦ, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τὸ ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, Καὶ τί δὴ τοῦτό ἐστιν; Ἐπίμεστον γὰρ τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ δόξης τὸ ἅγιον ἡμῶν θυσιαστήριον. Ἐν εἴδει δὲ τοῦ πυρὸς ἡ θεία τε καὶ ἀπόῤῥητος εἰκάζεται φύσις. Ἔοικε δὲ καὶ μυστικόν τι ὁ λόγος εὖ μάλα παραδηλοῦν. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τὸ ποῖόν τι φής; {ΚΥΡ.} Ἦ οὐκ αὐτὸν εἶναι τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ τὸ θεῖον ἐλέγομεν, ὡς ἐν τύπῳ, θυσιαστήριον, δι' οὗ προσίεμεν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, λατρεύοντες λογικῶς, καὶ μονονουχὶ καταθύοντες τὸ εὐῶδες ἐν ἀρεταῖς, καὶ τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας τὸν ἁγιασμόν; «Παραστήσατε γὰρ τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν, θυσίαν ζῶσαν, ἁγίαν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ὑμῶν.»
pass_a_gloss: Cleverly then the law, from what was accustomed to happen to them, sets the divine ministers upright toward the better, and as from a bodily type leads to spiritual contemplation. 'For you shall not go up,' he says, 'by steps upon my altar, so that you may not uncover your shame on it.' That is: the divine minister sanctified for my ministry, let him seek the lowly things, let him not leap up to the high. Let him decline boastfulness, so that he may not be seen unseemly and without beauty. For without beauty and wholly unseemly and very grievous a sickness of mind is the overswollen thinking. 'For the greater you are,' he says, 'so much humble yourself, and before the Lord you will find favour.' And the disciple of the Saviour also writes: 'Let the lowly brother boast in his height, and the rich in his lowering.' For he will pass away equally with the grasses, and will differ in no way from the flowers in the fields. PALL.: I agree. CYR.: So he said the minister must be freed of swelling and disdain. And in what way he would make the sacred service most lawful and unrebukable, you will know wholly clearly; for it is written in Leviticus: 'And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the whole burnt offering; this whole burnt offering on its burning upon the altar the whole night until the morning; and the fire of the altar shall burn on it, it shall not be quenched; and the priest shall put on a linen tunic, and he shall put on linen leg-coverings about his body, and he shall take away the offering wholly consumed, which the fire consumes, the whole burnt offering, from the altar, and he shall set it beside the altar; and he shall take off his robe, and put on another robe, and he shall carry out the consumed offering outside the camp to a clean place; and fire upon the altar shall burn on it and shall not be quenched; and the priest shall burn wood on it morning by morning, and he shall pile on it the whole burnt offering, and shall put on it the fat of the peace offering; and fire shall burn continually on the altar, it shall not be quenched.' Continual then and wholly unceasing is the fire of the altar, and not alien or from outside, but its own, that is, the one from above and from heaven. And what is this? For our holy altar is full of the glory of God. And in the form of fire the divine and ineffable nature is likened. And the saying seems also to hint very well at something mystical. PALL.: What sort of thing do you say? CYR.: Were we not saying that Emmanuel himself is, as in a type, the divine altar, through whom we draw near to God and the Father, serving rationally, and all but sacrificing the fragrance in virtues, and the holiness of the evangelical way of life? 'For present your bodies, a living sacrifice, holy, well-pleasing to God, your rational worship.'
pass_b_english: Cyril: So the law wisely takes what usually happened among them as a starting point to raise the divine ministers to something better, and leads them, as it were from a bodily type, to spiritual contemplation. For ‘you shall not go up by steps to my altar,’ it says, ‘so that you may not uncover your nakedness on it.’ (Exodus 20:26) That is: Let the divine minister who has been consecrated for my service seek what is lowly and not leap up to the heights. Let him renounce boastfulness, so that he may not be seen as shameful and unlovely. For arrogance is utterly unlovely and shameful, and a most grievous sickness of the mind. ‘The greater you are,’ it says, ‘the more you must humble yourself, and you will find favor before the Lord.’ (Sirach 3:18) And the Savior’s disciple also writes: ‘Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation, and the rich in his humiliation.’ (James 1:9–10) For the rich man will pass away like the grass and will differ in no way from the flowers of the field (James 1:10–11).

Cyril: So he said that the minister must be free of pride and disdain. And how he may perform his sacred service in the most lawful and irreproachable way you will learn with full clarity, for it is written in Leviticus: ‘And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the whole burnt offering. The whole burnt offering shall stay burning on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall burn on it; it shall not be put out. The priest shall put on a linen tunic, and he shall put linen undergarments on his body; and he shall take away from the altar the burnt portion of the whole burnt offering, which the fire has consumed, and set it beside the altar. Then he shall take off his robe and put on another robe, and carry the burnt portion outside the camp to a clean place. And the fire on the altar shall burn on it and shall not be put out; the priest shall burn wood on it every morning, lay the whole burnt offering in order on it, and place on it the fat of the peace offering. And fire shall burn on the altar continually; it shall not be put out.’ (Leviticus 6:8–13) The fire of the altar, then, is continual and wholly unceasing; and it is not foreign or brought from outside, but its own, that is, the fire that is from above and from heaven. And what does this mean? Our holy altar is filled with the glory of God, and the divine and ineffable nature is pictured in the form of fire. But the passage also seems to hint, and very aptly, at something mystical.
Palladius: What do you mean by that?

Cyril: Were we not saying that Emmanuel himself is, as in a type, the divine altar, through whom we draw near to God the Father, offering spiritual worship and all but sacrificing the fragrance of the virtues and the holiness of the gospel way of life? For ‘present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual worship.’ (Romans 12:1)

choices.why: κατακάρπωσις rendered 'burnt portion' (what the fire has consumed); τὸ στέαρ τοῦ σωτηρίου rendered 'the fat of the peace offering' (LXX 'of the deliverance/salvation offering').
λογικῶς / λογικὴ λατρεία rendered 'spiritual worship' both times, so the echo of Romans 12:1 stays visible (also 'reasonable/rational').

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 12 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Leviticus 6:8–13 in English Bibles is Leviticus 6:1–6 in the LXX and Hebrew. κατακάρπωσις rendered 'burnt portion' (what the fire has consumed); τὸ στέαρ τοῦ σωτηρίου rendered 'the fat of the peace offering' (LXX 'of the deliverance/salvation offering'). Sirach 3:18 numbering is the same in Rahlfs and NRSV. 'Pass away like the grass … flowers of the field' is Cyril's paraphrase of James 1:10–11 (compare Isaiah 40:6–7), cited as a clear allusion. λογικῶς / λογικὴ λατρεία rendered 'spiritual worship' both times, so the echo of Romans 12:1 stays visible (also 'reasonable/rational'). 'Fire from above and from heaven' may recall Leviticus 9:24 and 'the divine nature pictured as fire' may recall Deuteronomy 4:24 / Hebrews 12:29; neither is quoted, so neither is cited. 'Were we not saying' points back to an earlier book where Emmanuel is read as the altar. 'Draw near to God' (προσίεμεν) echoes Hebrews 7:25 loosely; left uncited.

Drafted Pass A, kept as written (rewritten as a literal English gloss from the Greek in pass_a_gloss): εὐφυῶς (cleverly/aptly) the law, ἀπὸ τοῦ συμβαίνειν αὐτοῖς εἰωθότος (from what usually happened to them), ἀνορθοῖ πρὸς τὸ ἄμεινον the θείους ἱερουργούς, and ὡς ἐκ τύπου σωματικοῦ leads πρὸς θεωρίαν πνευματικήν. Ex 20:26 again. τοῦτ' ἔστιν: the divine ἱερουργός ἡγιασμένος for my λειτουργία, ζητείτω τὰ ταπεινά, μὴ ἀναθρωσκέτω πρὸς τὸ ὑψοῦ (not leap up high). παραιτείσθω τὴν ἀλαζονείαν, lest ἀσχήμων ὁρῷτο καὶ ἀκαλλής. ἀκαλλὲς καὶ ἄσχημον κομιδῇ and παγχάλεπον ἀρρώστημα νοῦ = φρόνημα τὸ ὑπέρογκον (swollen mind/arrogance). Sir 3:18 (ὅσῳ μέγας εἶ, τοσούτῳ ταπείνου σεαυτόν, ἔναντι Κυρίου εὑρήσεις χάριν). the Saviour's μαθητής writes Jas 1:9-10 (καυχάσθω ὁ ἀδελφὸς ὁ ταπεινὸς ἐν τῷ ὕψει αὐτοῦ, ὁ δὲ πλούσιος ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει). παρελεύσεται ἐν ἴσῳ πόαις (pass like grasses), differ κατ' οὐδένα τρόπον from field flowers. PALL.: σύμφημι. CYR.: ὄγκου καὶ ὑπεροψίας ἀπηλλάχθαι δεῖν the ἱερουργός. how ἐννομωτάτην καὶ ἀνεπίπληκτον he makes ἱερουργίαν, εἴσῃ σαφῶς; written in Leviticus: Lev 6:1-6 LXX (= Eng 6:8-13): law of ὁλοκαύτωσις on its καῦσις on altar all night till morning; fire of altar burns, οὐ σβεσθήσεται; priest puts on χιτῶνα λινοῦν and περισκελὲς λινοῦν; ἀφελεῖ τὴν κατακάρπωσιν (removes the burnt portion) which fire consumes, from altar; sets it beside altar; ἐκδύσεται στολήν, puts on another; ἐξοίσει outside παρεμβολή to clean place; fire burns, not quenched; priest burns ξύλα morning by morning, στοιβάσει (stacks) the ὁλοκαύτωσις, places τὸ στέαρ τοῦ σωτηρίου; fire διὰ παντός on altar, not quenched. ἐνδελεχὲς καὶ ἀκατάπαυστον the altar's fire, οὐκ ὀθνεῖον ἢ ἔξωθεν but its own, τὸ ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ. what is this? ἐπίμεστον τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ δόξης our holy θυσιαστήριον; ἐν εἴδει πυρός the θεία καὶ ἀπόρρητος φύσις εἰκάζεται. the word seems μυστικόν τι παραδηλοῦν. PALL.: τὸ ποῖόν τι φής; CYR.: did we not say Emmanuel himself is the divine θυσιαστήριον ὡς ἐν τύπῳ, δι' οὗ προσίεμεν τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί, λατρεύοντες λογικῶς, μονονουχὶ καταθύοντες τὸ εὐῶδες ἐν ἀρεταῖς and τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας τὸν ἁγιασμόν? Rom 12:1 (παραστήσατε τὰ σώματα θυσίαν ζῶσαν, ἁγίαν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ, τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν).
